nodes.name: Receive status change
nodes.notes: POST /webhook/join-status. Allowed Origins (CORS) lists the domains the board is served from; without them the browser discards the answer although the call itself succeeded. Check the list against the real deployment - a wrong entry fails in the browser while curl keeps working.

nodes.name: Guard: verify, throttle
nodes.notes: Secret against $env.JOIN_NOTIFY_SECRET, required fields, the five valid status values, and a cap of 3 mails per ticket and day in /home/node/.n8n/join-notify-state.json. Everything that fails leaves as route=rejected.

nodes.name: Passed the guard?
nodes.notes: route=ok reads the ticket, everything else answers 403. The throttled case lands here too - a caller that hammers the endpoint gets the same bare answer as a wrong secret.

nodes.name: Fetch task
nodes.notes: The recipient address is read from the database, never from the request. Taken from the body, this webhook would be an open mail relay: the secret ships inside the delivered client code, so anyone holding it could have mail sent to any address. Coming from the record, the workflow can only ever write to the creator of a ticket that exists.

nodes.name: Build mail
nodes.notes: Only an external creator with an address gets a mail; internal members see the change on the board (Lastenheft). Everything else leaves as route=skipped.

nodes.name: Notify creator?
nodes.notes: route=ok sends the mail, route=skipped answers 200 without sending. A skipped notification is not an error - most tickets have an internal creator.

nodes.name: Send status mail
nodes.notes: Assign the SMTP credential after the import. Port 587 with STARTTLS - Hetzner blocks 25 and 465 outbound, and on 465 the node hangs until the execution timeout instead of reporting an error.

nodes.name: Respond: ok
nodes.notes: The client ignores the answer - it fires the webhook and forgets it. These three responses exist for debugging by hand.

nodes.name: Respond: skipped
nodes.notes: Not an error: the ticket has no external creator with an address, so no mail was due.

nodes.name: Respond: rejected
nodes.notes: Wrong secret, missing or unknown fields, a non-change, or the daily cap. The reason stays in the execution log on purpose - the answer must not tell a caller which check it tripped.
